column2: Launching a cheaper version of its flagship phone may cannibalize sales of the original model.
column3: 推出旗艦手機的平價版本，可能會蠶食原款機型的銷量。
column4: cannibalize existing sales (蠶食既有銷量)
column5: cannibal 食人族的字根：自己吃自己的產品，別嚇到小朋友

column2: Cannibalization explained why the new yogurt flavor did not raise total revenue; it simply replaced the old one.
column3: 自家產品互蝕解釋了為何新口味優格沒有提高總營收：它只是取代了舊款。
column5: cannibalize 加 tion：自家商品互搶客人的現象
column7: can - ni - bal - i - za - tion

column2: Mobile payment penetration in the region has reached ninety percent of adults in only five years.
column3: 該地區的行動支付滲透率在短短五年內就達到成年人口的百分之九十。
column5: penetrate 的名詞：產品像水滲進海綿裡有多深

column2: The brewer hopes to penetrate the Asian market by partnering with local convenience store chains.
column3: 這家啤酒商希望藉由與當地便利商店連鎖合作，打入亞洲市場。
column5: pen 像筆尖：筆尖戳進紙裡，產品鑽進市場

column2: Competitive pricing helped the small airline win customers away from its much larger rivals.
column3: 有競爭力的定價幫助這家小型航空公司把客人從大得多的對手那裡搶過來。
column4: a competitive price (有競爭力的價格)
column5: compete 競爭 + itive：拿出來能跟別人比一比的實力

column2: Rising labor costs have weakened the competitiveness of our factories compared with those overseas.
column3: 勞動成本上升，削弱了我們工廠相對於海外工廠的競爭力。
column5: competitive 加 ness：在賽跑中跑得多快的能力

column2: High licensing fees create a barrier that keeps small firms from entering the telecommunications market.
column3: 高額的執照費用形成一道障礙，使小公司無法進入電信市場。
column4: a barrier to entry (進入障礙)
column5: bar 横桿：橫著擋在入口的柵欄

column2: The railway held a monopoly on freight until the government allowed private companies to compete.
column3: 鐵路公司壟斷貨運，直到政府允許民間公司加入競爭。
column5: mono 單一 + poly 賣：整個市場只有一個賣家

column2: Regulators feared that the merged firm would monopolize the market for hospital software.
column3: 監管機關擔心合併後的公司會壟斷醫院軟體市場。
column5: monopoly 加 ize 使：把整個市場一個人包下來

column2: An oligopoly of three carriers controls most mobile service, so prices rarely fall much.
column3: 由三家業者組成的寡占掌控了多數行動通訊服務，因此價格很少大幅下跌。
column5: oligo 少數 + poly 賣：只有少數幾家賣家

column2: A cost overrun of forty percent forced the city to scale back the stadium project.
column3: 百分之四十的成本超支，迫使市政府縮減體育場計畫。
column5: over 超過 + run 跑：花費一路跑過預算的終點線

column2: Capital expenditure on new machines rose sharply this year, while daily operating spending stayed flat.
column3: 今年新機器的資本支出大幅上升，而日常營運開銷則維持不變。
column5: ex 出去 + pend 花費：錢從口袋飛出去的那筆錢

column2: Raising enough capital to buy the first fleet of delivery vans took the founders nearly a year.
column3: 籌到足夠的資本來購買第一批送貨車，創辦人花了將近一年。
column5: cap 像 captain 頭：企業最重要的頭號本錢

column2: Total revenue fell last quarter even though the number of customers stayed roughly the same.
column3: 儘管顧客人數大致維持不變，上一季的總營收仍下降了。
column5: re 回 + venue：錢從門口流回公司的總收入

column2: The grocery chain's inventory turnover is high, since fresh produce rarely stays on the shelves for long.
column3: 這家連鎖雜貨店的存貨週轉率很高，因為新鮮蔬果很少在貨架上待很久。
column5: turn 轉 + over：貨物在倉庫轉一圈進出的速度

column2: Amortization of the patent spreads its purchase price evenly across the twenty years it is protected.
column3: 專利的攤銷是把其購買價格平均分攤到受保護的二十年中。
column5: a 向 + mort 死：成本一年一年慢慢減少到零

column2: The firm will amortize the software license over five years instead of deducting the full cost at once.
column3: 公司將在五年內攤銷軟體授權費，而不是一次扣除全部成本。
column5: amortization 的動詞：把大筆費用切成小塊分次吃掉

column2: Depreciation of the delivery trucks reduced the company's reported profit by two million dollars.
column3: 送貨卡車的折舊使公司的帳面利潤減少了兩百萬美元。
column5: de 下降 + preci 價格：車子越開價格越往下掉

column2: Most laptops depreciate quickly, losing nearly half their value within two years of purchase.
column3: 大多數筆電貶值很快，購買後兩年內就損失近一半的價值。
column5: de 下降 + preciate 價格：價格往下滑的溜滑梯

column2: Despite strong profits, the firm faced a liquidity crisis because most of its money was tied up in unsold stock.
column3: 儘管利潤強勁，公司仍面臨流動性危機，因為大部分資金困在賣不掉的存貨裡。
column5: liquid 液體 + ity：錢像水一樣能馬上流動使用

column2: Cash and bank deposits are liquid assets, while a factory building cannot be sold quickly.
column3: 現金與銀行存款是高流動性資產，而工廠廠房無法迅速賣出。
column5: liquid 是液體：像水一樣說換就換成現金

column2: Rating agencies assess a bank's solvency by checking whether its assets exceed everything it owes.
column3: 評等機構透過檢查銀行資產是否超過所有負債，來評估其償債能力。
column5: solv 像 solve 解決：債務能解決還清的實力

column2: The retailer was declared insolvent after it failed to repay loans that had come due.
column3: 這家零售商在無法償還到期貸款之後，被宣告無力償債。
column5: in 不 + solvent：債務解不開，還不起錢

column2: Insolvency forced the family business to sell its building and negotiate with its creditors.
column3: 無力償債迫使這家家族企業賣掉大樓，並與債權人協商。
column5: in 不 + solvency 償債：欠的錢多過手上有的

column2: To survive, the airline had to restructure its debt and cut several unprofitable routes.
column3: 為了生存，這家航空公司必須重組債務並砍掉幾條不賺錢的航線。
column5: re 再 + structure 結構：把積木拆開重新搭一遍

column2: Following the restructuring, three divisions were merged and the head office moved to a smaller building.
column3: 重整之後，三個部門被合併，總公司也搬進較小的大樓。
column5: restructure 加 ing：公司積木拆開重搭的這個過程

column2: The synergy between the two firms meant their combined sales exceeded the total of their separate results.
column3: 兩家公司之間的綜效，意味著合併後的銷售超過各自單獨成績的總和。
column5: syn 一起 + ergy 工作：一加一大於二的團隊合作

column2: Designing the app and the speaker together was synergistic, since each product made the other more useful.
column3: 把應用程式與喇叭一起設計具有協同效應，因為每個產品都讓另一個更有用。
column5: synergy 加 istic：一起工作時力量變得更大

column2: Diversification into mobile games protected the publisher when sales of its older console titles declined.
column3: 當舊款遊戲主機產品銷量下滑時，跨足手機遊戲的多角化經營保護了這家發行商。
column5: diverse 多樣 + ification：雞蛋別放同一個籃子
column7: di - ver - si - fi - ca - tion

column2: Smart investors diversify their holdings across stocks, bonds, and property rather than betting on one sector.
column3: 聰明的投資人會把持有的資產分散到股票、債券與不動產，而不是押注單一產業。
column4: diversify the portfolio (分散投資組合)
column5: diverse 多樣 + ify 使：讓籃子裡的蛋有各種樣子

column2: The acquisition of a smaller rival gave the software giant access to its patents and customers.
column3: 對一家較小對手的收購，讓這家軟體巨頭取得了其專利與客戶。
column5: ac 向 + quis 尋求：向外把別家公司拿到手

column2: The retailer plans to acquire two regional chains, which would double the number of its stores.
column3: 這家零售商計畫收購兩家區域連鎖店，這將使其門市數量翻倍。
column5: ac 向 + quire 尋求：伸手把東西抓回來變自己的

column2: Shareholders approved the merger of the two banks, which created the nation's third-largest lender.
column3: 股東批准了兩家銀行的合併，這創造出全國第三大的放款機構。
column5: merge 的名詞：兩家公司像兩條河匯成一條

column2: The two rival airlines will merge next spring and operate under a single brand name.
column3: 這兩家敵對的航空公司將在明年春天合併，並以單一品牌營運。
column4: merge with a rival (與對手合併)
column5: 像汽車匯流道 merge：兩條車道合成一條

column2: The conglomerate decided to divest its hotel business so it could focus on its core manufacturing operations.
column3: 這家大型企業集團決定剝離旅館事業，以便專注於核心製造業務。
column5: di 離開 + vest 衣服：把不想要的衣服脫掉丟開

column2: The divestment of the struggling toy division raised enough cash to pay off the company's short-term debt.
column3: 出售經營不善的玩具部門所得的撤資款項，足以還清公司的短期債務。
column5: divest 脫掉 + ment：把包袱脫掉賣出去的這個行動

column2: The firm used the industry leader's delivery times as a benchmark when setting its own targets.
column3: 公司設定自己的目標時，以業界領導者的送貨時間作為基準。
column5: bench 長凳 + mark 記號：在長凳上刻刻度當標準

column2: Through benchmarking against the best hotels, the chain discovered that its check-in process was twice as slow.
column3: 透過與最佳飯店對標，該連鎖飯店發現自己的入住流程慢了一倍。
column5: benchmark 加 ing：拿最強的對手當尺，量自己差多少

column2: Centralizing procurement lets the hospital negotiate lower prices by ordering supplies for all its clinics at once.
column3: 集中採購讓醫院能一次替所有診所訂購用品，進而談到更低的價格。
column5: pro 為了 + cure 照料：為公司張羅所需的東西

column2: The factory struggled to procure enough steel after the main supplier shut down its plant.
column3: 主要供應商關閉工廠後，這間工廠很難籌集到足夠的鋼材。
column5: pro 為了 + cure 照料：想辦法把原料弄到手
